name: Naturpark Kaunergrat
kurzbeschreibung: Naturpark Kaunergrat enchants with the protected Piller Moor peat bog, the modern Naturparkhaus at Gachenblick, and the towering Wildspitze peak.
preis: Nature park and theme trails freely accessible; Naturparkhaus exhibition fee applies (approx. €7)
oeffnungszeiten: Park accessible year-round; Naturparkhaus open daily May to October and December to April
beschreibung:
Overview

The diverse Naturpark Kaunergrat spans a fascinating high-alpine nature park covering nearly 550 square kilometers between the Upper Inn Valley, the Pitztal, and the Kaunertal in the Tyrolean Oberland. Named after the jagged, glaciated Kaunergrat ridge crowned by the 3,768-meter Wildspitze, Tyrol's second-highest mountain, the park's elevation ranges from sun-drenched dry grassland at 750 meters up to eternal ice above three thousand meters. This dramatic altitudinal gradient fosters an extraordinary array of alpine habitats: fragrant stone-pine forests, ancient peat bogs, dry floral slopes, and untamed glacial streams that shelter rare plants such as the carnivorous sundew and endangered animals like the alpine ibex. The architectural and interpretive focal point is the Naturparkhaus perched dramatically atop Gachenblick on the Piller Höhe pass.

Route & Requirements

Naturpark Kaunergrat stands out as an exemplary European benchmark for inclusive, barrier-free alpine nature tourism. Directly at the Naturparkhaus begins the accessible trail to Piller Moor: a 1.5-kilometer raised timber boardwalk leads completely level and step-free through one of Central Europe's best-preserved peat bogs, allowing wheelchair users and strollers to observe rare bog plants up close (walking time approx. 1 hour, very easy). For seasoned mountaineers, the extensive trail network features demanding alpine routes, including climbs to the Rüsselsheimer Hütte or traversing the Cottbus High Trail. Sturdy mountain boots with grippy rubber soles and weatherproof clothing are essential for alpine trekking within the park boundaries.

Visit & Arrival

The award-winning Naturparkhaus on the Piller Höhe is located right on regional road L17 connecting Fließ in the Inn Valley with Wenns in the Pitztal, offering ample parking for cars and coaches. Public transit travellers arrive by rail at Landeck-Zams station and board regional bus 4232, stopping directly outside the centre. The building hosts the interactive exhibition '39.60 Degrees Nature-Art-History' and a panoramic restaurant.

Tips

Walk out onto the cantilevered Adlerblick viewing platform at the Naturparkhaus for a sensational perspective plunging over the Inn Valley before exploring the mystical Piller Moor. In the restaurant, sample regional dishes made with ingredients sourced directly from local nature park farmers.
